generation.exact_submitted_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, speech, chants or human voice. Exactly 96 seconds, 100 BPM, 4/4, playful and buoyant but gentle enough for repeated play. Original paper-sky jumping-game music in D major with a warm added-sixth color: light marimba, plucked/pizzicato strings, soft rounded synth bass, delicate shakers, brushed taps and restrained whimsical electronic percussion. A compact memorable bouncing motif, clean transients, open mids that leave room for short game effects, moderate density, cheerful upward motion without tension or excessive loudness. Arrangement: 0–24 seconds introduce the full loop groove immediately; 24–48 seconds add one light answering phrase; 48–72 seconds vary texture while keeping the same pulse; 72–96 seconds return seamlessly to the opening groove. Stable repeating loop body; no long intro, final cadence, dramatic ending, fade-out, silence, or tempo change. Final timestamp 96 seconds. Clean professional stereo mix, no clipping. Do not imitate a named artist, song, album or existing soundtrack. Instrumental only, no vocals

prior_inspection.measurement_command_note: Replace FILE with each delivered audio filename. The loudnorm report input_i/input_tp/input_lra measure the input file; its discarded normalized output is not a deliverable. Duration is also calculated from decoded sample frames / sample rate. PCM RMS aggregates both channels.

runtime_loop_boundary.interpretation: Sample continuity and edge energy are technical indicators only; they do not establish beat, harmonic or perceptual seamlessness.

observed_limitations: Generation did not meet the exact 96-second instruction: both files decode to 94.249795918 seconds, approximately 1.750204 seconds short. Duration was not forced by adding silence or altering the composition or tempo.

The ending has a pronounced low-energy tail. The runtime final 0.5 s is -54.3213 dBFS RMS versus -20.8143 dBFS RMS at the opening; approximately the last 0.849796 s stays below -40 dBFS in 10 ms RMS windows. The opening has approximately 0.08 s below that threshold. A repeated full-file playback may therefore have an audible energy dip or gap.

The decoded last-to-first sample jump is very small (-104.8538 dBFS), but this does not prove rhythm, harmony or perceptual loop continuity. Seamlessness is not established, and this is not certified as a production-ready seamless loop.

The untouched source measures +0.41 dBTP and has 43 decoded channel samples at or above full scale. MP3 reconstruction can cause overshoot, so this is not conclusive proof of pre-encoding clipping. Gain reduction yields a runtime measurement of -5.41 dBTP with zero decoded samples at or above full scale, but cannot undo distortion already baked into the source.
The requested 100 BPM, 4/4, D major, instrumentation and absence of voice were prompted but not independently verified by perceptual listening or music transcription.
prior_inspection.recommended_next_action: Audition the OGG end-to-start twice in the existing game before integration, paying attention to the low-energy tail. Any loop-boundary editing would require a separate decision; no second generation is authorized or performed.
